question:
The function $f(x)=\tan^{-1}(-x)+\frac{\pi}{2}$ is obtained from $y=\tan^{-1}x$.

(i) Describe the transformations involved.

(ii) Express $f(x)$ using $\tan^{-1}x$ and determine its range.

(iii) Find $f(0)$. Do not draw the graph.
explanation:
Reflection and translation
Replacing $x$ by $-x$ reflects the graph of $y=\tan^{-1}x$ in the $y$-axis. Adding $\frac{\pi}{2}$ then translates the reflected graph upward by $\frac{\pi}{2}$ units.

Odd-function property
The inverse tangent function is odd, so $$\tan^{-1}(-x)=-\tan^{-1}x.$$ Hence, $$f(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}x.$$

Range transformation
The range of $\tan^{-1}x$ is $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Negation preserves this interval, and adding $\frac{\pi}{2}$ gives the range $$(0,\pi).$$

Value at the origin
At $x=0$, $$f(0)=\tan^{-1}0+\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}.$$

options.A: Reflection in the $x$-axis followed by a downward shift of $\frac{\pi}{2}$; $f(x)=-\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}x$; Range: $(-\pi,0)$; $f(0)=-\frac{\pi}{2}$
options.B: Reflection in the $y$-axis followed by an upward shift of $\frac{\pi}{2}$; $f(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}+\tan^{-1}x$; Range: $(0,\pi)$; $f(0)=\frac{\pi}{2}$
options.C: Reflection in the $y$-axis followed by an upward shift of $\frac{\pi}{2}$; $f(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}x$; Range: $(0,\pi)$; $f(0)=\frac{\pi}{2}$
options.D: Reflection in the $y$-axis followed by a downward shift of $\frac{\pi}{2}$; $f(x)=-\frac{\pi}{2}+\tan^{-1}x$; Range: $(-\pi,0)$; $f(0)=-\frac{\pi}{2}$
